english: They're just lazy boys.
A good kick can get a man going.
But it can just as easily cause him to resist a good piece of advice.
Our service to the city is not something you can put a price on.
Great comeback. Bet he's thought about that one for a long time.
Uh- yeah. It is.
They're awfully quiet.
I'm actually, uh... I work on Waterlane. On some days.
The magic kid raises his hand. "I used to deliver milk. It's a seasonal thing."
Rollo worked at the Fishery.
He gives the quiet kid a dirty look. "Those assholes fired me for not keeping up a bullshit quota."
So yeah, Cleric. We would have proper jobs if this city wasn't so infected.
Infected with what?
R-"I can recommend you boys into the Urthguard."
Good luck with that.
Uh. Outsiders? Freestriders?
You mean immigrants?
I, too, dislike immigration.
Calling anyone not from Norvik an infection is horrible.
I- sometimes. But not like-
Y-yeah. Or, I mean- it's not like everyone coming here is bad.
That's not what I-
I have a friend from Fordnip. He's cool.
And Likki's family is Vourgeni. There's a difference between immigrants and immigrants.
Who are the 'good immigrants' in this case?
We should have more immigration. That'll solve all our problems.
Only humans should be allowed in Norvik.
Only humans and dwarves should be allowed in Norvik.
Only humans and dwarves should be allowed in Norvik. And halflings.
(Wait for the kid to explain.)
The... types that work hard. I guess?
Don't commit crimes.
They should learn to speak Diminor too.
When they make nice food.
Cool. We've got a definitive list now.
He scoffs, loudly.
That's... no?
Then there'd be even less jobs for us Urthfolk.
That's not how economic growth works.
Yeah, but there'll be lots of happy non-Urthfolk.
The Urthfolk don't deserve to exist anymore. We should all just disappear into the void.
Uh. Okay, maybe not. But that doesn't change what it's like to work for the guilds today.
Sure. At the expense of us? Like, what the hell?
He stares at you with a stunned expression.
You- you want us to die?
If you're going to complain too darn much, yeah!
Sounds a bit rough when you put it like that.
He shakes his head. "Well, I do not agree."
Thanks.
He rubs his cheek.
A nervous tic.
It's... complicated, okay?
Norvik has always been a place Urth conquered for humans. But he was also friends with lots of other folk.
So the main issue isn't really immigrants. It's more like... when there's so many immigrants that the city can't really keep everyone, like...
Happy?
Prosperous?
Safe?
Politically engaged?
Fed?
Housed?
Employed?
In stable long-term healthy relationships?
Sure, something like that.
But in the end, the Freestriders make a bunch of crowns in the city. While the Urthfolk suffer.
And we don't like that.
We don't.
We really don't.
Really don't?
The Freestriders bring prosperity to all. The Urthfolk will be better off. Eventually.
It sounds like you dislike the greed of Reeds more than you dislike immigrants.
The Freestriders bring democracy and stability. That comes at a cost.
I think we should keep things exactly as they are now.
Just get a job. How hard could it be?
Really don't.
The silent kid mutters, "We don't."
We do not.
We disagree.
Yes! That's exactly it!
He's so happy not having to feel like a racist.
Well, we can't afford that cost.
Okay. We disagree.
Easy for you to say.
Have you tried getting a gig at any of the guilds in the last couple of years?
Seventy hours a week at the fishery got me barely enough to afford rent. Add some food on top of that, and it's barely enough to survive.
And then they cut the hourly rate, to keep up with pressure from investors. You know, from Reeds.
It's a shitshow.
Thanks.
...What?
The blonde kid looks at you with confused, darting eyes.
It has not sunk in yet.
Yeah. You'd get fast-tracked into training.
The kid starts muttering to himself.
Intense fear suddenly washes over him.
But that's...
(Point at the kid who keeps casting cantrips.) "And you could be a cleric one day."
The lanky boy begins to speak, but stops himself.
He realizes you are correct. And he appears frightened over the possibility.
(Take out some paper and write them an official recommendation each.)
They look stunned as you hand over the papers to them.
Are you serious?
Urthguard? Isn't that... clerics?
Lots of different Urthguard. From Street Watchers to Equestrians. You'd make a great Wall Enforcer, big guy.
Oh. Wall Enforcer? Like, with armor?
Huh. I thought only nobles could be Equestrians.
No, they changed that. Read about it in the paper. Though being a Street Watcher seems like a bit of a shit job...
As his friends speak, the blonde kid looks at his recommendation in disbelief.
So, this is...
More bodies into the machine.
Careful. If you put them into the system, they won't get a chance to continue this 'Resistance'.
The boys will make fine warriors.
Of course, if you fail, they might reject the whole idea.
Want to get rid of them? Just appeal to their dreams.
These kids probably won't listen. But... maybe?
Just trust them to make a decision themselves.
Not so unemployed anymore!
Convince them to join.
A job. Take it or leave it.
These boys are idiots.
But they're stubborn idiots. Perfect for boot camp.
Just make it clear that they can do all of their political bullshit from inside the system.
It's time for you to put your beliefs to the test, boys.
They all look at you.
The system is broken. But it can only be fixed by those with power. Power within the city itself.
You want us to-
I need you to join the Urthguard. That's the only way you'll ever get enough influence to change this city.
I can't just-
Guess I could? Dad would be happy if I got a stable job.
Yeah, it's not such a bad idea...
Do we get armor?
(Tap him on the shoulder.) "As much armor as you can carry."
...Hell yeah.
Hm.
Be careful. If you don't want them running off and joining straight away, that is...
Your quest will be failed if you send them off.
Maybe tell them to wait. Or you'll lose the quest...
Give it time. Mull it over, it's a big decision. (Have them stick around. For now.)
Go. Right away. The Urthguard awaits! (Get rid of them.)
Okay. We will.
Thank you, Lord Cleric. He bows his head.
Unfortunately, so are you.
What? That's rude.
Sorry, but it's true.
Actually, not sorry.
Because you have no idea how to convince these boys.
That's not true. I have an idea.
Yes. You do.
Unfortunately.
(Grab Rollo by the shoulders.) "You're not a pussy, are you?"
The boy doesn't say anything. He just looks at you.
The boys seem to recoil physically when you use this strange term.
Thank you for helping all women find a place in this world.
Thank you for using the word in a more positive connotation.
You will make the next generation of boys better.
Don't be a... wimp.
He says nothing.
...Chicken. (Squawk.)
No, Lord Cleric.
But we'll consider it. Okay?
Okay... (Hold back tears.)
It's a good deal. My dad would love it.
But uh... I'll have to ask.
Same.
If I get armor, it would be cool...
Rollo gestures to his buddies. "We'll think about it. Thank you, Lord Cleric."
I'll think about it. We all will.
Uh. Thanks, Cleric. Lord Cleric. He bows his head.
Uh. Okay!
Fine. You guys... wanna go?
I'll... become a cleric? Isn't that really hard?
Yes. Only the best can become clerics. You have to do your best.
(Shrug.) "I could do it."
Oh boy.
Huh. Right.
I guess so?
I'm gonna get armor. Awesome.
Just head to the recruitment office in the Palace.
Alright.
Uh. See you, Lord Cleric.
One by one, they shuffle out of the rollermill with nervous expressions on their faces.
E-Let's hope they do well in training.
Sure. Hit me!
Kid's a maso-chitic, eh? Go for it.
If you insist. (Ready a punch.)
(Look to the others.) "All of you. I need the truth."
What? No! Stop!
Hit me with a question! Any question!
Ah. That makes a lot more sense.
We'll tell you anything we know.
The quiet kid nods.
Where were you on the day of the explosion?
What do you know about the tea shop's owner?
You ever hang out in the tea shop?
That's all for now.
I was home.
What about you? (Point at the lanky kid who keeps casting fire cantrips.)
You were all home, then? During lunch? On a work day?
He clears his throat. "I was at Toli's place. His dad can vouch for it."
And if I did have the power to cause explosions like that, I wouldn't use it to blow up a tea shop.
Even if it was an Azgal rat-hole.
A very weak motive, yes. Even if he was a secret Beast of Jor, or something akin.
Suspicious.
They nod.
Well.
My little brother was close though. Thank Urth he didn't get hurt.
He told me about the fire being weird, or something. Probably magical.
So yeah. Esoteric bullshit.
He works in the kiosk on Pillar Road.
Some birdfolk. I don't know. Never talked to the guy.
The rest of you?
They shrug collectively.
No. Of course not.
It was an Azgal hangout. Modissa was there a lot, from what I understand.
Bet she knows a lot about it.
Great. Just say the word if you need anything else.
Rollo. Is that a nickname? Because you hang out in a rollermill?
Where'd you grow up?
Why'd you join this 'movement'?
What does your father think of you being in this 'movement'?
Alright. No more personal questions. I know enough.
No. That's just my name.
Mm. Weird choice.
...Good name.
I don't believe in coincidences.
It's a very normal Urthfolkian name.
I have two uncles named the same.
I believe you.
Sure. Whatever you say, kiddo.
...Two?
He sighs.
Over on Wall Street.
You're lucky you made it out alive.
Cool place.
Was it nice there?
It's not that bad. I think.
Not really. It's way too cramped.
Eh. A bit cramped, but not that bad.
We lived in an apartment right at the river.
Stuff happened, and then we moved to Tolstad. Not that big of a difference, to be fair.
My little brother likes it better here though. So that's good.
Because my city needs me.
Right? he asks his friends, who all nod in approval.
So you're not just bored and looking for an outlet?
An honorable cause.
The city doesn't need you, kid. Stop playing around.
He looks guilty.
He is guilty.
I agree!
He scoffs. "We're not playing."
Considering he's dead, I don't think he cares too much.
I'm sorry for your loss.
What about your mother?
He shrugs. "Don't be. He was an asshole."
I'll ask her if she comes home this month.
Look, it's me and my brother. Alone. Okay?
It's fine. We both work.
Do I like milk?
That's what I asked, yes.
I... I guess?
(Face the others, one by one.) "Does anyone here - any one of you - partake in the glory of milk-drinking?!"
Don't look at me.
Uh...
I dabble?
Then I will offer you this one opportunity: one bottle of milk for two thousand crowns!
...No thank you.
They all reject your offer, both body-language-wise and facial-expression-wise.
Eh. I tried.
You really, really did.
Sure?
He gives you a confounded - frankly idiotic - look.
Instead, we'll go for more non-personal questions.
E-"No more questions at all, in fact."
...Okay?
Yeah. If you can.
It might be a bad idea, but...
It might also not be. I just have a feeling.
She holds her head high. In silence.
You see the halfling looking around the room, as if searching for any sense of threat from the boys.
The dwarf girl is trembling.
We shouldn't be here, Modissa...
She waves off her friend's concern. "Rollo!"
What's your fucking deal?
My deal?
Yeah. What's your problem?
Everyone, let's calm down.
Don't get all hysterical, Modissa. Let's just talk.
She's got a point, Rollo. Maybe you should apologize.
(Don't say anything. Just observe.)
Calm down? This piece of shit's been hounding us for months.
And now he wants to talk? Like, what the hell.
Hysterical?
Hysterical?
Usually there's no clear good or bad choice in a dialog like this.
But that was, objectively, the wrong thing to say.
For once - agreed.
First off- fuck you, she says and gives you the finger.
Secondly, fuck you guys too, she says and moves her middle finger towards the boys.
You've been hounding us for months, and now you want to talk?
Apologize?
What is this? What do you want?
You- he says, and stops himself to let out a frustrated laugh.
You, Modissa - and your friends, he says, pointing at Xerba and Jehanne. "You're indoctrinated."
That's a big word, Rollo. You learn that yesterday?
WE...! he yells, before lowering his voice, "We have some information."
Information? the dwarf girl pipes up in the back.
We... do actually.
Yeah, you should shut up and listen to Rollo for once, Modissa.
Modissa crosses her arms and grunts out, "Okay."
Speak.
Rollo glances to you.
Then he says, "We got our hands on a secret document detailing the sale of Waterlane."
She laughs.
What are you guys talking about?
It's true, the short boy pipes up in the corner.
They're selling the whole thing. To Freestriders.
Modissa's mocking laugh goes silent.
Show me.
You have to promise me you'll-
Show me, Rollo.
Fine.
The girl carefully grabs the ledger from Rollo as he hands it over.
As she flips through the pages she asks, "How many copies have you made?"
The boys look at each other.
Oh gods be good... she mutters and stares at the fine print, adjusting her glasses.
Was that my job? Did I forget?
Holy shit...!
The normally silent dwarf girl suddenly exclaims some profanity and puts a hand over her mouth.
That's the Magistrate's sigil...!
What? You're kidding...
Modissa slowly looks up from the papers and glares at Rollo.
Where did you find this, Rollo?
He points at you.
I got it from the Askanii-Reeds Trading Company headquarters. On Waterlane. I can vouch for the information inside.
Huh.
So you stole it.
Wasn't what I was looking for necessarily, but yes.
Nothing compared to the riches they steal from the working class, eh? (Wink.)
She shows an expression of disgust at your overt pandering.
It's ours now. And we need a way to spread the information.
Hold on. You want us to print it in The Chant?!
Well. Yeah.
She clicks her tongue and looks at Xerba, then Jehanne. They both shrug.
The Chant is illegal anyway. What are they gonna do, arrest you?
It's not that I'm worried about, dumbass.
I'm thinking about the exposé I'll be writing on this.
Modissa!
Wait, what do you mean?
I'll write one and put it in The Chant. Duh.
Hold on, I asked for your help because I wanted you to spread the information. Like, send it out to a bunch of newspapers.
The Chant is the best paper in the city!
It's also the smallest.
My parents have never heard about it.
That's... actually relevant, Sten. Yeah, like- no one normal knows about The Chant!
You can write whatever you want, but you also need to send it out to other papers!
She scoffs. "Just so they can ignore it all, because they don't want to piss off their investors."
You guys clearly have no idea how this stuff works.
But... won't it be safest to send it out, just in case? And also write that article?
Modissa grumbles to her friend, "Just hold on..."
Look, we need to get a good spread here.
Then it'll just get lost in the noise!
We need a... a spearhead!
We do!
(Try to think.)
Modissa wants her big story.
Rollo doesn't know what he is talking about here. But his heart is in the right place.
The psychological effect here is the most important thing to consider.
Would people care about the voice of a small unsupported newspaper?
Would the big papers bite more or less if The Chant wrote about it first?
Then again, it's more about whether it comes out before or after the election too...
Before, of course!
But it's pretty soon. Isn't it?
Modissa, Rollo speaks up, cutting through the noise.
Give me back the documents.
The Azgal girl grips them harder.
Tense.
Such a boring debate.
Just sell the papers! Get rich!
They need to understand each other.
Then they will find a compromise.
Just take a stand. Take CONTROL.
They need a leader. BE ONE.
Make them understand each other.
Force through your opinion.
Two lines. Go.
Modissa.
She looks at you, still gripping the documents.
Rollo was the one who suggested to talk with you.
Huh? Really?
She squints at you.
You'll get to write your article. But you need to take everyone's opinion in mind here.
Rollo produces a conspicuous sound.
Rollo. The Azgal Youth obviously know more about printing than you do. Listen to them. They know what they are doing.
Both sides look at you.
A compromise can be found.
Modissa will write her exclusive. On the day of the election, when the article is out, you make sure copies of the document are delivered to the other publications. Win-win.
You share the documents immediately, so every major paper gets a chance to write articles on it for election day. Modissa- your article will stand out with some exclusive details.
This is not going to cut through.
You simply do not have the ability to understand them well enough yourself.
Must be the age.
I'm not that old.
Not yet.
What's that supposed to mean?
Cleric?
Oh. (Look at them.)
She sighs.
GO!
BE LOUD! BE PROUD!
EVERYBODY, <shake>SHUT THE FUCK UP</shake>!
They look at you, stunned.
Excuse me?
Listen up. You're clearly not ready for this responsibility- arguing like little kids.
Hey, we're just-
Shut up. The adult is talking.
Modissa sighs.
But she listens.
You get angry. You get... raged.
Listen to me!
Give me the documents. NOW!
Oh, like I gave all the newspapers to you?
The ones you burned? Fuckhead?
LISTEN!
None of them do.
They just keep arguing.
THEY.
JUST.
KEEP.
ACTING.
LIKE.
ANNOYING.
LITTLE.
BRATS.
(Slam your head into the ground.)
The smash makes a loud ringing sound echo down the Rollermill.
They stare at you, stunned.
What the fuck are you doing?
Fine. Right?
Rollo lays eyes on his companions for a few seconds, just to make sure they agree. They all nod.
Good. Great. I'm okay with that.
I'll make the copies. Since you clearly can't be arsed.
Then I'll release my article at the same time as all the other papers. If they actually end up writing anything. Which I doubt.
Is that a good enough compromise?
Rollo lays eyes on his companions for a few seconds, just to make sure they agree- then he nods.
Let's do it.
It's a deal.
We can trust her, right? Sten asks, pointing at Modissa.
Oh, this boy. So blunt.
Yeah, Rollo replies with a shrug.
I think so.
She puts the documents in order in the ledger. "Of course you can trust me."
We have the same enemies.
Uh. Yeah, I guess we do, don't we?
Duh.
The Freestriders.
They're destroying the city. Selling it out.
Ruining the working class' only chance at a stable life.
A good income. My dad is working overtime all the time.
Mine too.
I think that's more a dad-thing, though.
Uhm... rent in apartments is too high too. Although that's more of an income problem too, I suppose...
It goes together. My parents were evicted last year, just because the landlord raised the rent twice in a year.
That was Dinkleberry, right? I've heard he's an asshole.
We need rent control laws! Housing shouldn't be some wild investment portfolio. The state needs to regulate it, or everyone suffers.
The Urthfolk suffer, you mean.
And halflings. And merfolk. And dwarves.
And goblins.
Of course.
They're finding common ground.
It's beautiful.
A union between radicals.
It's both awesome and horrifying.
The point is, in short, Capital needs to be taken down.
Capital?
She pauses, adjusts her glasses, then elaborates.
...The ones with money.
Ah. Yeah, that's a good start.
Hold on now just a damn second...
Are the kids talking shit?
Agreed. Go eat the rich, kids.
A coalition for the ages. I believe this calls for a huzzah.
Just focus on this corruption business, and don't mingle too much. If you young people get too organized, things might actually change in the city. Like, fast. Scary fast.
You're lucky I'm apolitical, or else this would have actually stirred some emotions in my cold, dead heart.
Modissa chuckles at your comment.
Eat the rich? You've got the Azgalist slogans down right.
Please don't.
Exactly. Don't.
A what?
LOUD AND CLEAR!
(Yell.) "<shake>HUZZAH!</shake>"
Oh gods.
Good gods.
Sure, huzzah!
Huzzah?
HUZZAH!
Yeah, Huzz-ah!
...Boys.
YES!
You're ruining them.
You're ruining these poor boys.
As you speak, you see the idea form in their heads.
OH NO.
THE BLOOD WILL FILL THE STREETS.
